ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there are two of the same right isosceles triangle ABC. Both figures show B as the right-angle vertex, AB vertical, BC horizontal, and AC is the hypotenuse from A to C. In Figure 1, one side of the square is on AB, one side is on BC, and the upper-right vertex of the square lies on the hypotenuse AC. In Figure 2, the square is tilted: one of its sides is along the hypotenuse AC, and the two endpoints of the opposite side parallel to it lie on AB and BC respectively. Reasoning: Let the lengths of the two legs of the right isosceles triangle be L, take coordinates B=(0,0), A=(0,L), C=(L,0), then the equation of the hypotenuse AC is x+y=L. In Figure 1, let the side length of the square be s, then its upper-right vertex is (s,s), on the hypotenuse, so 2s=L. It is known that the area of the square in Figure 1 is 441, therefore s=21, so L=42. In Figure 2, let the endpoints of the side of the square that lies on AB and BC be (0,p) and (p,0). The length of this side is p√2, and it is parallel to the hypotenuse AC. The corresponding other side is on AC, and its endpoints are (p,2p) and (2p,p). These points satisfy x+y=3p, therefore 3p=L=42, giving p=14. The area of the square in Figure 2 is (p√2)^2=2p^2=2·14^2=392.

method.method_draft: Use similar triangles and altitudes. From the image, identify ABC as a 45-45-90 triangle. In Figure 1, the square is placed at the right-angle corner B with sides parallel to AB and BC, so the remaining small triangle above/right of the square is similar to ABC; equivalently, in an isosceles right triangle the aligned square side is half the leg length. The text gives the Figure 1 square area as 441, so its side is 21 and the triangle leg length is 42. For Figure 2, read that the square has one side along the hypotenuse AC and the opposite side parallel to AC with endpoints on the two legs. Let the Figure 2 square side be t. The altitude from B to AC in the large 45-45-90 triangle is 42/√2. The square contributes perpendicular width t, and the smaller 45-45-90 triangle between B and the inner side of the square has hypotenuse t, hence altitude t/2. Therefore 42/√2 = t + t/2 = 3t/2, so t = 28/√2 = 14√2. The area is t^2 = 392.

Image description: In the attached figure there are two of the same right isosceles triangle ABC. Both figures show B as the right-angle vertex, AB vertical, BC horizontal, and AC is the hypotenuse from A to C. In Figure 1, one side of the square is on AB, one side is on BC, and the upper-right vertex of the square lies on the hypotenuse AC. In Figure 2, the square is tilted: one of its sides is along the hypotenuse AC, and the two endpoints of the opposite side parallel to it lie on AB and BC respectively.

Reasoning: Let the lengths of the two legs of the right isosceles triangle be L, take coordinates B=(0,0), A=(0,L), C=(L,0), then the equation of the hypotenuse AC is x+y=L. In Figure 1, let the side length of the square be s, then its upper-right vertex is (s,s), on the hypotenuse, so 2s=L. It is known that the area of the square in Figure 1 is 441, therefore s=21, so L=42.

In Figure 2, let the endpoints of the side of the square that lies on AB and BC be (0,p) and (p,0). The length of this side is p√2, and it is parallel to the hypotenuse AC. The corresponding other side is on AC, and its endpoints are (p,2p) and (2p,p). These points satisfy x+y=3p, therefore 3p=L=42, giving p=14. The area of the square in Figure 2 is (p√2)^2=2p^2=2·14^2=392.
